newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-London Clubs look abroad after DTI blow.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-London Clubs look abroad after DTI blow.

text.p: Casino operator London Clubs International (LCI) plans to build up its overseas operations after the UK government blocked its plans to acquire Capital Corporation Plc.

LCI chief executive Alan Goodenough told Reuters overseas operations accounted for less than 10 percent of business but that LCI aimed for a 50/50 split within two or three years. LCI turnover was 179.5 million stg in the year to end-March.

LCI has seven casinos in the UK capital plus one in France, one in Egypt and one in Beirut. He said the company was completing arrangements for a casino in Las Vegas and pitching for a licence at Niagara Falls and two in South Africa.
The UK government said on Tuesday it would not permit LCI's proposed hostile bid for Capital Corporation as the enlarged company would control some 80 percent of up-market casino business in London.
"The manner of the rejection is disappointing as their analysis of the industry is flawed," said Goodenough.

He dismissed claims that a deal would have allowed LCI to reduce the quality of services and raise charges. He said that the charges at gaming tables were centrally regulated, not under the control of individual companies.

The UK may grant casino licences in up to 20 new locations as part of a planned deregulation of the industry. Goodenough said LCI, which has no UK operations outside London, may seek licences in areas around the capital such as Croydon, Oxford and Slough.
